html:
The Citadelle Laferriere is a huge mountaintop fortress in northern Haiti, built from 1805 to 1820 under Henri Christophe to guard against a French return. It is the largest fortress in the Americas.

Christophe, a general of the revolution, ruled the north after the death of Dessalines, and in 1811 made himself King Henry I. Thousands of labourers built the fort and his palace of Sans-Souci below it. The Citadelle was armed with over a hundred cannons.

The French never came. Christophe, partly paralysed by a stroke and facing revolt, shot himself in 1820. The Citadelle and Sans-Souci became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982, a symbol of the nation born from the declaration of 1804.
